publications.title: The AI Written RFP: what five engines tell buyers to require in fourteen software categories
publications.abstract: First public research release covering all 14 software categories: 2,003 criteria, 10,547 requirement spans, 2,417 explicit criterion and vendor associations, and 10,015 vendor page comparisons. The derived answer base is 2,093. Research completion and publication checks pass. Team review: in progress. Zero statements are represented as analyst verified. No synthetic captures or reviewer identities are included. This release includes the complete data tables, a 30-page report, the independent verifier and SHA256 integrity manifest. Source answers were captured on 22 to 23 Sep 2026 under method v1.1 and remain deposited at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695. Perplexity quotation text is omitted; exact source identifiers, offsets and hashes remain for verification. Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1. https://broadcastwell.com/methodology CC BY 4.0. Any named company may request one no-cost re-run at index@broadcastwell.com; both results are published.

publications.title: A Systematic Overview on AI Music Generation, Arrangement, and Orchestration
publications.abstract: The rapid growth of AI-based music generation, arrangement, and orchestration has resulted in a large and fragmented body of literature, making it increasingly difficult for researchers and practitioners to navigate recent developments and identify the most promising approaches. Existing surveys often focus on specific subfields or do not fully reflect recent advances such as diffusion models, transformer-based architectures, and large-scale commercial systems. This thesis addresses these gaps through a systematic literature review reported with reference to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, investigating AI methods for music generation, arrangement, and orchestration published between 2020 and 2025. From 4,521 records identified across six academic sources, 1,083 could be exported to Zotero for record management and screening; after deduplication and eligibility assessment, 107 primary studies were included in the review. For each included study, information regarding methodology, datasets, musical representations, evaluation procedures, performance metrics, and code availability was extracted and organised in a comprehensive comparison table. The review extends the taxonomy proposed by Zhu et al. (2023), synthesises eight major research trends, and identifies and justifies 27 systems for in-depth analysis, whose available demonstrations and outputs are examined through a pilot exploratory listening analysis, and whose author-reported evaluations are synthesised separately. The contributions include an updated taxonomy of AI music systems, a structured comparison of 107 studies, a trend analysis spanning 2020–2025, and practical recommendations for future research in AI-assisted music generation, arrangement, and orchestration.

publications.title: Modeling collective action in POM: The Strategy–Operations–People framework
publications.abstract:
While many business situations relevant to production and operations management (POM), such as supply chain coordination or sustainable operations, involve some form of collective action; managerial frameworks for collective action rarely appear in POM contexts. Valuable insights may thus be missed, reducing the effectiveness and implementability of the proposed POM solutions. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a framework for collective action that has its roots in the organizational behavior literature. We formalize it mathematically not only to offer definitional clarity, but also to relate it to common POM modeling approaches. We then illustrate its relevance to POM by mapping it to case studies in supply chain coordination and sustainable operations. The proposed framework, named the Strategy–Operations–People (SOP) framework, is structured in three levels, comprising three elements, two elements, and one element, respectively. First, the
                    Strategy
                    level induces and enforces solidarity among all team members by specifying common goals, shared values, and well-defined rules. Second, the
                    Operations
                    level organizes the decentralized execution of collective action in autonomous subgroups through a detailed specification of roles and processes. Third, the
                    People
                    level requires the individual commitment of all team members to the proposed collective action program, since a team’s performance rests on the individual contributions of its members. The framework thus addresses the common, subgroup, and individual dimensions of collective action. The SOP framework also contributes to the broader fields of team leadership and organizational behavior in two ways. First, its mathematical formalization brings operational clarity on the defining scope of the framework’s elements. Second, mapping the framework to two problems in supply chain management and sustainable operations illustrates its broad applicability, moving beyond collective action within organizations, to guide collective action taking place across organizations.

publications.title: Integrasi Workflow Jurnal Keuangan Berbasis Website Menggunakan Analisis Pieces dan Metode Agile Scrum
publications.abstract: Hospital financial governance depends on how well the journal approval workflow is recorded and traced. The desktop-based Financial Information System (SIMKEU) used by the hospital under study supports journal entry and posting, but examination, approval, and endorsement are still handled through physical documents outside the system, so access is inflexible and the process status is not digitally documented. This study analyses the running system and develops a website-based financial information system that integrates the tiered journal workflow. Data were collected through observation, interviews with finance staff, the assistant finance manager, and the finance manager, and a literature study. The running system was analysed using the PIECES framework, while development applied the Agile approach with Scrum over approximately three months, with the researcher acting as a single full-stack developer. The system was built on CodeIgniter 3 and combines the existing Oracle database as the journal data source with MySQL as the workflow, access-rights, and activity-log store, so the legacy schema remains unchanged. Alpha testing of twenty function groups using black-box testing produced conforming results, and User Acceptance Testing with five respondents produced an acceptance rate of 76.89% in the Good category.

publications.title: FAIR Research Data Management with NOMAD and FAIRmat
publications.abstract: These slides accompanied an invited tutorial presented at TCO 2026 on 28 September 2026 in Leipzig, Germany. The presentation introduces NOMAD, a free, open-source research data management platform developed and operated by FAIRmat, a consortium of the German National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI). NOMAD enables researchers to upload, organize, explore, analyze, and publish their data. By transforming heterogeneous research data into structured, machine-readable formats, the platform helps make them findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR). The presentation provides an overview of relevant concepts, tools, and practical workflows for managing materials-science data throughout the research lifecycle. It covers data upload and automated processing, metadata extraction and enrichment, schema-based data modelling, data organization, search and exploration, analysis, and publication. It also introduces NOMAD’s support for experimental and computational data and discusses how structured, contextualized datasets can be prepared for machine-learning and artificial-intelligence applications. Both NOMAD deployment options are presented: the publicly accessible central platform and NOMAD Oasis, a customizable infrastructure that research groups and institutions can host and operate independently. The slides are intended for researchers, developers, and research-data professionals interested in interoperable data infrastructures, reproducible research, and applying the FAIR principles to computational and experimental materials science.

publications.title: e2er (End-to-End Research)
publications.abstract: e2er is the open infrastructure for publishing, verifying, reproducing and reusing AI-enabled research. Templates describe research processes as a sequence of steps. Each template organizes specialists, i.e., AI agents with defined roles, and each specialist draws on skills, i.e., written descriptions of methods. Researchers can adjust any template, specialist, or skill and publish their version for fellow researchers. Researchers decide at which steps the process pauses for their review. A study produced with e2er comes with a dossier that helps others verify and reproduce the work and attributes everyone whose templates, specialists, and skills it used.

publications.title: Security Lab Automation: network security validation workstation for emulated end-to-end network labs
publications.abstract: First public release of Security Lab Automation, the network security validation workstation used on the Linux hosts of an isolated EVE-NG end-to-end lab. Author: Medardo Jairo Suntaxi Cocanguilla (MSc, C|EH) Developed in a personal home lab and used for postgraduate security and networking practice. Lab context An automated service-provider topology (IS-IS/MPLS/LDP core, BGP route reflectors, PE with VRF, CE with VRRP, DHCP and NAT) runs on EVE-NG. Once the network is operational, each Linux host (Ubuntu1, Ubuntu2, Alpine) runs security_lab.sh. The lab is isolated from the Internet by default and scans are limited to lab hosts. Features Interactive menu (10 options) and tool check with install hints. Tests: ping, fping, DNS (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, PTR), whois, nmap (top 100 TCP ports with version detection, -sT -T2), HTTP/HTTPS headers, TLS certificate and traceroute. Input validation (IP or DNS name only), per-command timeouts, authorized-target notice. TXT report per run with command log and summary. Tkinter edition with JSON export. Student security practice guide: reconnaissance across the MPLS core, service enumeration, ACL before/after validation, lab web services. License: MIT

publications.title: Saying 'Hi'. What goes around comes around
publications.abstract: This proposal presents, under the rather grand name of “hypotheses,” observations drawn from a brief experiment I conducted about 12 years ago and my experiences with neighbors. Before uploading it to Zenodo, I did a quick AI-assisted search of scholarship on “Saying Hi to Strangers” in Korea. It seems that research on the “really real strangers” I encountered is still scarce. So, as I find more of my old records, I plan to upload them under the same title, with different version numbers. The versions currently planned are as follows:Version 01 – The Hypotheses – The first thing I'm curious aboutVersion 02 – The Effects of Repeated GreetingsVersion 03 – Cross-National Differences and Prior ContactVersion 04 – A Conversation with a Trail Maintenance WorkerVersion 05 onward – To Be Determined

publications.title: Scripting WebArena: A Language-Model-Free Agent at 77.7%
publications.abstract: LK-47.web is a WebArena agent with no language model and no learned weights. A grammar maps each task intent to one of the benchmark's 190 template identifiers and its slot values, and a hand-written plan of site skills carries the task out through the original, unmodified harness. The plans were written against the test intents, so the agent is an expert system for these templates and makes no claim to transfer to other tasks. In one run on 9 October 2026 it passed 631 of 812 tasks (77.71%), with the 84 tasks that need the harness's GPT-4 judge counted as failures. Of the 95 graded failures, 65 are tasks whose reference answer or grader disagrees with the site or the intent, and earlier work flagged 27 of them independently. Three are timing faults and 27 are the agent's own. The paper lists all 65 disputed tasks with their reasons. Code: https://github.com/LK-maker-007/LK-47.web, commit f815cd8, MIT licence. Per-task results, the runner's ledgers and all 812 trajectories: https://github.com/LK-maker-007/LK-47.web/releases/tag/run-2026-10-09 Files: the paper (PDF, 10 pages).
